rule: The teeth sit on the maxilla and mandible, which form a rounded surface; the teeth wrap around it and the line where upper and lower teeth meet follows that curve rather than a flat horizontal.
The upper lip recedes into the skull from top to bottom, so under light from above it falls into shadow.
Construct a young, beautiful face with as few lines as possible; extraneous lines read as wrinkles and age the subject.
On a beautiful face the nose can be a single line defining the lower edge of the nostrils and tip.
A cast shadow starts with a dark, hard edge next to the object casting it and softens as it moves away.
A lit sphere shows highlight, light, halftone, core shadow (the darkest area) and reflected light on the shadow side.
A shadow cast from one form onto another pushes the receiving form back in space.
Age shows as gravity on the face: sagging cheeks and jowls, shadow under cheekbones and jaw, sunken sockets and droopy lids.
Asymmetry suggests chaos; symmetry suits calm or orderly characters.
A limb nearer the viewer is drawn larger than normal, with overlapping diagonals, so it comes out of the picture plane.
Drapery follows five fold types - single-point hanging, dual-point hanging, compression, zigzag, spiral - each set by its support points, the form beneath and gravity.
